newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Summit project shows wide zones of uranium.
newsitem.headline: Summit project shows wide zones of uranium.

text.p: Summit Gold NL said on Friday drilling results from its Valhalla project in northwest Queensland had revealed wide zones of uranium mineralisation.
The mineralised intersections, between 250 and 320 metres below the surface and from 22 to 31 metres in width, confirmed the vertical continuity of the deposit, Summit said.
"All three diamond core holes intersected wide zones of uranium mineralisation," Summit said.
Brokers said the grades were much higher than expected, resulting in a sharp re-evaluation of the share price.
By 10.05 a.m. (2105 GMT) Summit was up 30 cents (78.95 percent) at NZ$0.68, but off its historical peak of NZ$0.75.
Summit and Resolute's drilling programme in the central portion of the deposit had delineated a drill inferred-resource of over 10 million tonnes containing in excess of 27 million pounds of U3O8.
"Importantly the deposit remains open in all directions," Summit said.
Valhalla forms part of the Mount Isa Exploration Joint Venture, which is a 50/50 venture between Summit and Resolute Ltd.
Core samples had been sent for metallurgical testing.
